TEN-218.title: [P1] A hung mirror POST blocks flush() for ever, so the T1 site upload never starts
TEN-218.description:
**What breaks.** The T1 upload awaits `flush()`, which returns the serialized sync chain. Because mirror requests have no timeout, one request that hangs rather than fails never settles the chain, and the upload never begins.

**Evidence.**
`apps/web/lib/data/siteUpload.ts:314-319`:

```ts
return getAttemptPersistence().flush().then(() => uploadSiteZip(storage, opts, clientAttemptId, zip));
```

`flush()` returns `this.inflight` (`lib/data/persistence.ts:199-201`), fed by `postJson` with no timeout and no signal (`persistence.ts:155-168`). The exam page then sits in `{ state: "uploading" }` (`app/exam/page.tsx:393-404`) and `SiteUploadNotice` offers a retry only in the error state.

**Blast radius.** Every hosted T1 completion behind a stalled connection. The candidate finishes the build they just made and the publish never ends and cannot be retried.

**Fixed when.** `flush()` is bounded, or the upload does not await it unboundedly, and a test with a never-settling fetch asserts a visible error with a retry.

TEN-123.title: Nothing wires onSyncError - a hosted sitting can fail to mirror for its whole duration, silently
TEN-123.description:
`apps/web/lib/data/persistence.ts:195` declares `onSyncError` and `:683` never passes one. So every mirror failure during a hosted sitting is swallowed.

`FRONTEND.md` §1: *"offline -> visible state"*. A candidate can sit a full run whose event log never reached the service, with nothing on screen saying so, and discover it only when the report cannot find their attempt.

Do: wire `onSyncError` in `browserApiOptions()` to a persistent, non-dismissable "not saved" indicator in the exam chrome, next to `PersistWarning`, and clear it on the next successful sync.

TEN-124.title: One SaveConflictError poisons persistence for the rest of the sitting
TEN-124.description:
`packages/session/src/persist.ts:60-70`. After a single `SaveConflictError` the persistence layer stops saving for the remainder of the sitting, locally and server-side, and the report then reads the stale `localStorage` log.

A candidate finishes a run and gets a report built from a log that stopped growing at the conflict - which is a score computed from partial evidence, presented as a score.

Do: recover rather than latch - re-read the stored log, re-derive from the current revision, and if the conflict cannot be resolved, stop the clock and say so instead of continuing to accept work that is not being saved.

TEN-259.title: [P2] Clerk tokens are verified with no authorizedParties, so azp is never checked
TEN-259.description:
**What breaks.** `verifyToken` is called with `secretKey` only. The `azp` claim is never checked, so any token minted by the same Clerk instance for any front end is accepted by this API. The service already knows the list it should pass.

**Evidence.**

* `packages/backend/src/clerk.ts:20-24`: `const payload = await verifyToken(auth.slice("Bearer ".length), { secretKey: this.secretKey });`
* Clerk's own guidance is to pass `authorizedParties` so a token issued for another front end cannot be replayed.
* The allowlist is already available as `AILX_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` / `allowed_origins` in `infra/terraform`.
* Today the same Clerk instance backs the public frontend and both staging deployments, and README section 7 records it is a DEVELOPMENT instance repurposed from another product.

**Blast radius.** Only matters once a second app shares the Clerk instance, which is exactly what a repurposed development instance means today.

**How we know it is fixed.** `verifyToken` receives `authorizedParties` built from `AILX_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, and a test asserts a token with a foreign `azp` is refused.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-259.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-258.title: [P2] funnel_events is anonymous-writable with three indexes and no retention
TEN-258.description:
**What breaks.** The funnel sink is the only route a stranger can write. The rate limit is per instance, so the real ceiling is multiplied by `max_instances`. Worst case is roughly 300/min x 20 rows x 4 instances, about 34M rows a day, into a table with three indexes, no partitioning and no retention job.

**Evidence.**

* `services/api/src/rateLimit.ts` `FUNNEL_SHARED_RATE_LIMIT = 300/min`, per instance and in-process (README section 2 states this).
* `infra/terraform/variables.tf` `max_instances = 4`.
* The per-address limit is inert because `AILX_TRUST_PROXY` is set nowhere in `infra/terraform` (`clientAddress` returns null without it).
* `db/schema.sql`: `funnel_events` carries three indexes and no partitioning; there is no retention job anywhere in the repo.
* Verified CLEAN: the step name IS a real Postgres CHECK constraint as the README claims, the insert is idempotent (`funnel_events_once`), and the row carries no IP, user agent, URL, referrer, account id or attempt id.

**Blast radius.** Storage and index bloat on the one table a stranger writes, plus autovacuum load on the shared database.

**How we know it is fixed.** A retention or partition policy exists for `funnel_events`, and the ceiling is stated as a global number rather than a per-instance one.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-258.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-257.title: [P2] The T1 GitHub export has no request timeout and leaves an empty repo when it hangs
TEN-257.description:
**What breaks.** The GitHub artifact export uses bare `fetch` with no `AbortController` anywhere, uploads up to 500 blobs in one request, and creates the repository FIRST with no compensating delete. A hang or a partial failure leaves an empty repository on the candidate's own GitHub account with no cleanup, and the export route has no rate limit.

**Evidence.**

* `packages/backend/src/t1/github.ts:206-224`: bare `fetch`, no `AbortController`. `grep -n AbortController packages/backend/src/t1/github.ts` returns nothing.
* Contrast `packages/backend/src/judging/model.ts:285`, which does use one, so the pattern is known in this repo.
* `packages/backend/src/t1/github.ts:499-520` creates the repo before any blob is uploaded; there is no delete on failure.
* `packages/contract/src/t1.ts` `T1_LIMITS.maxFiles = 500`.
* The route carries no rate limit (see the authenticated rate-limit finding).

**Blast radius.** A candidate's own GitHub account gets an empty repo, and the request occupies an instance until the socket dies.

**How we know it is fixed.** Every GitHub call carries an `AbortController` with a budget, a failed export deletes the repo it created or creates it last, and a test with a hanging server shows the handler returning inside the budget.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-257.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-256.title: [P2] Migrations run in one transaction with non-concurrent CREATE INDEX and full-table backfills
TEN-256.description:
**What breaks.** Migrations are applied `singleTransaction` with no `lock_timeout`. They contain full-table backfills and non-concurrent `CREATE INDEX`. That is safe on today's small tables and becomes a deploy-time stall that blocks every write once the tables are real-sized, because the migrate job runs before the traffic switch.

**Evidence.**

* `db/migrate.ts` applies with `singleTransaction`; no `lock_timeout` is set (see the related timeout finding).
* `db/migrations/0012_*.sql` backfills every `share_links` row with an `UPDATE`.
* `db/migrations/0007_*.sql` scans all of `responses`.
* `db/migrations/0009` through `0013` create indexes without `CONCURRENTLY`.
* The migrate job runs to completion before the Cloud Run traffic switch (`infra/cloudbuild/release.sh`), so a stalled migration is a stalled deploy with the old revision still serving.
* Verified CLEAN: migrations are forward-only with unique numeric prefixes and a `checkOrder` gate; the baseline path verifies every relation before fake-recording `0000`; new constraints on existing tables are added `NOT VALID` (`0002`, `0008`); `0008`'s DELETEs copy verbatim to `archive.*` first, have a working Down, and abort via `RAISE EXCEPTION` if a credential holder is ever in scope.

**Blast radius.** A future migration on a large table blocks writes for its whole duration, inside a deploy window.

**How we know it is fixed.** The migrate session sets a `lock_timeout`, index creation is `CONCURRENTLY` outside the single transaction, and a backfill on a large table is batched.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-256.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-255.title: [P2] AILX_REVIEWERS is set by no deployment, so no share carrying a site or a note can ever be listed
TEN-255.description:
**What breaks.** A share that carries a T1 site or a candidate note needs a human stamp before it is listed. The reviewer allowlist is an environment variable that no deployment sets, and there is no Terraform variable for it, so `isReviewer` is false for everybody and the queue can never be worked. Appeals in the moderation thread can never be answered either.

**Evidence.**

* `packages/backend/src/gallery.ts` `REVIEWERS_ENV = "AILX_REVIEWERS"`; `reviewerRefs` fails closed on unset; `gallery.ts:556-568` `withReviewer` returns 403 to everyone.
* `grep -rn AILX_REVIEWERS` finds only `README.md`, tests and `gallery.ts`. It is absent from `infra/terraform/run.tf` `runtime_env` and there is no variable for it in `variables.tf`.
* `packages/contract/src/share.ts` `needsHumanApproval(payload)` returns true when `site !== null` OR `note !== null`; `packages/backend/src/share.ts` `publishShare` auto-stamps only when `!needsHumanApproval`.
* `services/api/src/app.ts:502-505` registers the review routes regardless.

Two more variables the code reads that no deployment sets: `AILX_INSTRUMENT_DIGEST` (unset makes the digest pin a no-op, `packages/instrument/src/index.ts:255-260`) and `AILX_TRUST_PROXY` (unset makes the per-address anonymous rate limit inert, `services/api/src/rateLimit.ts` `clientAddress`).

**Blast radius.** Every candidate who opts their build or their note into the gallery. They see `submitted`, for ever, with no reviewer able to exist.

**How we know it is fixed.** `AILX_REVIEWERS` is a Terraform variable wired into `runtime_env`, at least one deployed environment names a reviewer, and `GET /v1/gallery/review` returns 200 for that identity.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-255.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-254.title: [P2] A gateway that answers with a different model id makes every judging re-run re-bill and double-count
TEN-254.description:
**What breaks.** The re-run skip compares the REQUESTED model id, but the stored row carries the ANSWERING model id, and the unique key includes `model_id`. Against a gateway that version-pins (for example `x/y` answering as `x/y-2026-01`), no re-run ever skips: every pass re-bills the jury AND writes extra rows, and the aggregate sums all rows for a dimension, so the score moves.

**Evidence.**

* `packages/backend/src/judging/worker.ts:291-292` skips on the requested id.
* `packages/backend/src/judging/worker.ts:307` and `packages/backend/src/judging/model.ts:341` store the answering id.
* `packages/backend/src/judging/store.ts:96-99` unique key includes `model_id`.
* `packages/core/src/judgments.ts:96-113` sums all rows for a dimension, so an extra row changes the aggregate rather than being ignored.
* The README states the opposite: "a retry re-uses the stored evidence and calls no model".
* Combines with the non-atomic lease and the re-claim loop, and there is no per-day spend alarm.

**Blast radius.** Judge spend and score stability on any gateway that does not echo the requested id verbatim. OpenRouter-style gateways commonly do not.

**How we know it is fixed.** The skip and the unique key use the same id, a re-run against a gateway that renames the model calls no model, and the aggregate is unchanged.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-254.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-253.title: [P2] assertJudgmentsAttested runs only in the browser, so the server checks no attestation on write
TEN-253.description:
**What breaks.** The attested-judgments invariant is enforced in the browser session engine and nowhere on the server write path. `judgmentIds` are written into the score row and are never recomputed or compared by any file in `packages/backend/src`. Nothing stops judgment rows being added after a score of record is issued, so a stored score can silently stop matching a recompute from stored inputs. This is the invariant that separates re-scoring from re-judging, and on this side of the boundary it is asserted, not enforced.

**Evidence.**

* `packages/backend/src/judging/worker.ts:362` and `packages/backend/src/finalize.ts:306` WRITE `judgmentIds`.
* `grep -rn 'assertJudgmentsAttested' packages/backend/src` returns nothing. The function exists only in `packages/session/src/machine.ts:257` and `:417` (the browser engine) and in tests.
* No file in `packages/backend/src` recomputes `judgmentId()` from stored rows and compares it to the claimed list on read.
* `judgments` has no constraint tying a row to a point in time relative to a `scores` row, so a later insert changes what a recompute would produce while the stored score stays.
* The order-invariance half IS enforced: `packages/core/src/judgments.ts` aggregates order-invariantly and the custody comparisons in `packages/backend/src/custody.ts` do run on both write and read.

**Blast radius.** Every judged score of record. The claim that any issued score is byte-identically recomputable from stored inputs is not checkable server-side today.

**How we know it is fixed.** The score write recomputes `judgmentId()` for each row it replayed and refuses a mismatch, `readScoresOfRecord` re-checks the same list, and a test that inserts an extra judgment after a score makes the read report the score unverifiable.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-253.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-252.title: [P2] Append-only is application discipline: the runtime connects as the table owner
TEN-252.description:
**What breaks.** The README calls `responses`, `transcripts` and `judgments` append-only. Postgres does not know that. There is exactly one trigger in the whole schema and it is unrelated, every table is owned by the same role the service connects as, and there is no INSERT/SELECT-only runtime role. The invariant is a code convention, and the code is one review away from breaking it.

**Evidence.**

* Live `pg_trigger` in schema `public`: exactly one trigger, `scores_track_recorded`. No append-only enforcement trigger and no rule exists on any table.
* Live `pg_roles`: only four login roles; only `ailx_admin_ro` is SELECT-only. All tables are owned by `neondb_owner`, and the service connects as the owner.
* Live `pg_stat_user_tables.n_tup_del` is non-zero on tables the README calls append-only or stable: `responses` 341, `attempts` 54, `participants` 52 (from migration `0008`, which does copy verbatim to `archive.*` first and has a working Down).
* The application half is clean: `grep` for `UPDATE`/`DELETE` against `responses`, `transcripts`, `judgments`, `practice_answers` or `moderation_comments` in `packages/backend/src` returns nothing. That is discipline, not a constraint.

**Blast radius.** The store's central claim. An auditor cannot verify append-only from the database alone.

**How we know it is fixed.** The service connects as a role with INSERT and SELECT only on the append-only tables (UPDATE granted per column where a lifecycle stamp needs it), and a manual `DELETE FROM responses` as the runtime role is refused.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-252.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-251.title: [P2] No database backup or PITR is provisioned or stated anywhere
TEN-251.description:
**What breaks.** The store is append-only and is the whole product. There is no database resource in Terraform at all, and no backup, PITR or RPO statement anywhere in the repo. Migrations are forward-only with `max_retries = 0`, so a bad migration has no documented recovery path.

**Evidence.**

* `infra/terraform/*.tf` declares no database resource; the database is the existing Neon Postgres (README section 7).
* `grep -rn 'PITR\|point-in-time\|backup' README.md docs/ infra/` returns two unrelated hits.
* `infra/terraform/judging.tf` and the migrate job use `max_retries = 0`.
* README section 7 already records that a future Cloud SQL move needs a `pg_dump` taken during a write freeze, because a snapshot taken while writes continue would silently drop rows. Nothing states the RPO today.

**Blast radius.** Total loss of every score of record, every judgment and every credential, with no stated recovery point.

**How we know it is fixed.** The Neon branch/PITR retention window is written down with an RPO, a restore is rehearsed once, and the runbook is in the README.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-251.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-250.title: [P2] The T1 snapshot bucket has no versioning and the runtime service account can delete evidence
TEN-250.description:
**What breaks.** T1 snapshots are the stored input a T1 score is replayed from. The bucket has no object versioning, no retention policy and no lifecycle rule, and the runtime service account holds `objectAdmin`, which includes delete. Byte-identical replay is therefore not enforced in storage: a bug or a compromise removes the evidence with no backstop.

**Evidence.**

* `infra/terraform/storage.tf` is 24 lines and declares no `versioning`, no `retention_policy` and no `lifecycle_rule`. `grep -rn versioning infra/terraform/*.tf` returns nothing.
* The runtime service account binding on the bucket is `roles/storage.objectAdmin`.
* README section 2 invariant: "A T1 snapshot is servable only while a `responses` row records its digest". That gate stops an orphan being served; it does not stop the bytes being deleted while the row remains.

**Blast radius.** Any T1 score whose snapshot is deleted becomes unreplayable, and the `responses` row still claims the digest.

**How we know it is fixed.** The bucket has versioning plus a retention policy, and the runtime SA holds `objectCreator` + `objectViewer` rather than `objectAdmin`.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-250.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-249.title: [P2] The runtime service account holds project-level secretAccessor, so the public API can read every secret
TEN-249.description:
**What breaks.** The service account that serves anonymous public traffic has `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` at the PROJECT level, not per secret. Any code execution or SSRF in the API image reads every secret in the project, including the one that seals every candidate's provider key. The correct pattern already exists next door: the deployer's grant is per secret.

**Evidence.**

* `infra/terraform/main.tf`, resource `runtime_secret_accessor`: the binding is on the project, not on individual secrets.
* Secrets in reach: `ailx-provider-key-secret` (seals every stored provider key under AES-256-GCM), `ailx-clerk-secret-key`, `ailx-judge-api-key`, `ailx-github-token` (a repo Contents write token), `ailx-database-url`.
* The deployer grant in the same file is scoped per secret, so the pattern is already understood in this repo.

**Blast radius.** Every stored provider key, the Clerk secret, the judge key and a GitHub write token, from one compromise of the public API image.

**How we know it is fixed.** The runtime grant is one `google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member` per secret the service actually reads, and `gcloud projects get-iam-policy` shows no project-level `secretAccessor` for the runtime SA.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-249.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-248.title: [P1] The startup probe reads /livez, so a misconfigured revision goes green and takes all traffic
TEN-248.description:
**What breaks.** The README claims the service refuses to start when `AILX_AUTH` is unset. It does not. `server.ts` binds the port first, and the pool, the auth provider, the snapshot store and the instrument are all lazy `??=`. The Cloud Run startup probe and the deploy smoke test both read `/livez`, which returns a JSON literal and touches nothing. `/readyz` does check Postgres and the bank and is used by neither. A revision with a broken config passes the probe, takes 100% of traffic, and `release.sh` has no rollback step.

**Evidence.**

* `README.md:337` claims an unset `AILX_AUTH` refuses to start.
* `services/api/src/server.ts:21-24` binds the port before any dependency is constructed. Lazy initialisation at `services/api/src/context.ts:116` and `:189`, `snapshots.ts:114`, `instrument.ts:34`.
* `services/api/src/app.ts:321` `/livez` returns a JSON literal.
* `infra/terraform/run.tf` `startup_probe` and `infra/cloudbuild/release.sh` both use `/livez`.
* MEASURED live: `/readyz` median 93 ms vs `/livez` 67 ms. The cost of using the correct probe is 26 ms.
* `infra/cloudbuild/release.sh` writes only the image and contains no rollback step.

**Blast radius.** Any deploy with a missing or wrong environment variable. The bad revision serves every request and the first symptom is a candidate's 500.

**How we know it is fixed.** The startup probe and the deploy smoke test read `/readyz`, and a revision deployed with `AILX_AUTH` unset fails to become ready instead of taking traffic.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-248.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-247.title: [P1] GET /api/site/:digest/* bypasses apiRoute, so it has no rate limit and takes one pool client per asset
TEN-247.description:
**What breaks.** The T1 site serving routes call `withApiContext` directly rather than going through `apiRoute`. They get no rate limit, not even the anonymous shared ceiling, and every asset of a hosted candidate site is one anonymous request, one Postgres round trip and one pool checkout. A site may carry up to 500 assets. This is the exact second-path pattern that <issue id="042ab382-b724-4b39-b8bd-f42f14cb0fad" href="https://linear.app/tenken/issue/TEN-107/two-public-pages-are-broken-on-staging-gallery-sends-a-query-the">TEN-107</issue> fixed for the share route, still open here. `/readyz` has the same shape.

**Evidence.**

* `services/api/src/app.ts` (route table at the end of `createApp`): the two site routes call `serveSite(...)`, and `serveSite` calls `withApiContext(...)` directly, not `apiRoute`.
* `packages/backend/src/t1/handlers.ts` `handleServeSite` runs one `SELECT 1 FROM attempt_site_claims WHERE digest = $1 LIMIT 1` per asset before the bytes are read.
* The share route's own comment in the same file records that this pattern was the <issue id="042ab382-b724-4b39-b8bd-f42f14cb0fad" href="https://linear.app/tenken/issue/TEN-107/two-public-pages-are-broken-on-staging-gallery-sends-a-query-the">TEN-107</issue> defect: a second path into the service with its own body handling and no rate limit.
* `packages/contract/src/t1.ts` `T1_LIMITS.maxFiles = 500`.
* `services/api/src/context.ts:112` `DEFAULT_POOL_MAX = 3`; `infra/terraform/variables.tf` `pg_pool_max` / `concurrency` = 8.
* `/readyz` is also anonymous and unlimited and runs `ctx.db.query("select 1")` on a checked-out client.

**Blast radius.** All candidates on the instance. One published gallery card that links a site, or one crawler, drains the pool; pool exhaustion 500s after the 10 s acquire timeout, so a sitting in progress fails to append its log.

**How we know it is fixed.** The site routes and `/readyz` go through one adapter that applies a limit, or the digest reachability check is served without a pool client, and a test asserts no route reaches `withApiContext` outside `apiRoute`.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-247.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-246.title: [P1] T3 transcript order is candidate-supplied seq, so a back-filled turn buys verification credit
TEN-246.description:
**What breaks.** T3 credit is order-sensitive and the order is `transcripts.seq`, which the candidate supplies for their own turns AND for the server-written `assisted` row. A candidate can insert a turn at an earlier free seq after the fact and buy credit for deliberation that never happened. `server_ts` exists in the schema and is never read. The store's own comment gives exactly this reason for not trusting `client_ts`, then orders by a column that is equally candidate-supplied.

**Evidence.**

* `packages/backend/src/store.ts` `getTranscripts` orders by `t.seq, t.id`. Its doc comment: "`client_ts` is candidate-supplied and a candidate who could reorder their own transcript could turn a blind accept into a deliberated one".
* `packages/backend/src/handlers.ts` `handleAppendTranscript` passes `b.seq` straight through; `store.ts` `assertSeq` checks only the integer range.
* `packages/backend/src/handlers.ts` `handleT3Assist`: `const seq = typeof b.seq === "number" && Number.isInteger(b.seq) && b.seq >= 0 ? b.seq : nextSeq(rows);` The client names the position of the row the SERVICE writes as its own evidence.
* `packages/track-t3/src/scoring.ts` `verificationTally` is index-order dependent: `const answerFinalAt = submittedAt < 0 ? transcript.length : submittedAt;`, `if (raisedAt === undefined || i <= raisedAt) return;`, `if (!stance || stance.at <= checkedAt) continue;`.
* Concrete sequence: post `assisted` at seq 10, `accepted` at seq 20, then insert `verified` at seq 15. The check now precedes the stance and counts as a discriminating verification.
* `transcripts.server_ts` is written and never read by any query in `packages/backend/src`.

**Blast radius.** Every T3 sitting, the 35-point Process component, and the reported reliance behaviour. This is a scoring-integrity defect on the store's central claim: only rows a request body cannot write are proof.

**How we know it is fixed.** The order scoring reads is server-observed (`server_ts` or a server-assigned monotonic sequence), the assist route stops accepting `b.seq`, and a test that appends a back-filled `verified` row asserts the tally does not move.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
TEN-246.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-245.title: [P1] No rate limit on any authenticated write route, including the 25 MB T1 upload
TEN-245.description:
**What breaks.** For a signed-in caller everything except score, finalize and the model proxy is unbounded: attempt creation, log appends, transcript appends, the 25 MB site upload, share and credential writes, practice starts, and the attempt read the browser polls every 5 seconds. There is no per-attempt row cap either, so one account can grow the append-only table that the anonymous aggregates route scans.

**Evidence.**

* `services/api/src/context.ts` `rateVerdict()`: for `identity !== null` the rule comes only from `opts.limit` or `opts.publicRead`; with neither it returns `null`, meaning no limit. In `services/api/src/app.ts` only `/finalize` and `/score` pass `SCORE_RATE_LIMIT` and the six `/v1/model/*` routes pass their own.
* `packages/backend/src/store.ts:800` inserts one row per request; the only bound is `MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES = 1024 * 1024` (`context.ts:52`) and `assertSeq` (`store.ts:83`), which accepts any non-negative 32-bit integer. So one attempt may hold up to 2^31 rows of up to 1 MiB.
* Live proof the client picks its own seq: `max(seq)` in `responses` is `1073741824` (2^30).
* `responses.payload` is `jsonb` with no size CHECK. `moderation_comments.body` and `profiles.display_name` are unbounded `text` in the database; `COMMENT_BODY_MAX` is applied only in `packages/contract/src/moderation.ts:126`.
* The upload is the worst case: `POST /v1/attempts/:id/site` is registered with `{ rawBody: true }` and no `limit`; `readCappedBody` buffers up to `T1_LIMITS.maxTotalBytes` = 25 MiB (`packages/contract/src/t1.ts:13`) into one array, and `packages/backend/src/t1/zip.ts` inflates it with `inflateRawSync` on the event loop of a 1-vCPU container, up to 500 entries.
* Nothing deletes: `responses`, `transcripts`, `practice_answers`, `moderation_comments`, `funnel_events` and `attempt_track_events` all document "never deleted" and there is no retention job in the repo.

**Blast radius.** One account can pin an instance's CPU with repeated uploads, and can make the public aggregates route arbitrarily expensive for everybody by growing `responses`.

**How we know it is fixed.** Every write route carries a rule, the polled attempt read carries one sized for the 5 s cadence, a per-attempt row ceiling exists, and a test enumerates the route table and fails on a write route with no limit (same shape as the existing public-route enumeration test).

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*

TEN-244.title: [P1] GET /v1/aggregates and GET /v1/gallery scan whole tables on every anonymous request and carry no cache header
TEN-244.description:
**What breaks.** The two public reads are unbounded full-table work on routes a stranger may call in a loop. `/v1/aggregates` selects EVERY `responses` row whose payload type is `attempt_started` or `track_scored`, with no LIMIT and no time window, sorts them, ships them to Node and JSON.parses each one, plus three more full-table aggregations. `/v1/gallery` runs about eight queries per page view, six of them full scans. Neither carries `Cache-Control` or `ETag`, so every page view costs a container and a pool client.

**Evidence.**

* `packages/backend/src/aggregates.ts:41` `SELECT attempt_id, payload FROM responses WHERE payload->>'type' = ANY($1) ORDER BY attempt_id, seq`. No LIMIT. Live plan: `Seq Scan on responses ... Filter: ((payload ->> 'type') = ANY (...))` then a Sort. No index exists on `(payload->>'type')`.
* Same handler: `aggregates.ts:97` explodes every `attempt_decks` row, `:123` groups all of `attempts` by week, `:140` runs three `count(*)`.
* MEASURED on a PGlite replay of `db/migrations` (40 log rows per attempt):

| attempts | responses rows | rows into Node | query time |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 2,000 | 80,000 | 4,000 | 28 ms |
| 12,000 | 480,000 | 24,000 | 180 ms |

Linear. 50,000 attempts projects to about 750 ms and 100,000 rows materialised per anonymous request.

* Gallery: `packages/backend/src/gallery.ts:237` listing, `:244` count, `:274` publishedCount, `:314` a `GROUP BY s.payload->'playerType'->>'code'` that no index can serve, `:345` a loop of four axis queries. `packages/contract/src/gallery.ts:217` caps `offset` at `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.
* MEASURED live: `/v1/gallery` 124 ms and `/v1/aggregates` 184 ms warm median, with only `vary: Origin` and no `Cache-Control` or `ETag`. Cold start for `/livez` was 7628 ms with `min_instances = 0`.
* The only ceiling is `PUBLIC_READ_SHARED_RATE_LIMIT = 600/min` per instance (`services/api/src/rateLimit.ts`), which is 10 requests/second against a 3-connection pool. The per-address limit is inert because `AILX_TRUST_PROXY` is set nowhere in `infra/terraform`.

**Blast radius.** Anonymous, no account needed. The wall and the world page are the growth surfaces, so this is the route real traffic hits first, and it shares the pool with every sitting.

**How we know it is fixed.** The aggregate is materialised or cached with a validator, `offset` is capped at a real page depth, the facets are one query, and the plan for both routes contains no `Seq Scan on responses` or `share_links`.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*

TEN-243.title: [P1] attempts.participant_id and judgments(attempt_id, track_id) have no index
TEN-243.description:
**What breaks.** Two tables that grow with every candidate are read on hot paths with a sequential scan. `attempts` is the parent every authenticated read reaches through; `judgments` is scanned up to three times per `GET /v1/attempts/:id`, which is the 5-second poll the report runs while judging is pending.

**Evidence.**

* `db/migrations/0000_baseline.sql` and `db/schema.sql` create no index on `attempts(participant_id)`. `judgments` has only `UNIQUE (submission_id, dimension, sample, rubric_version, model_id)`, which cannot serve a lookup by `attempt_id`.
* Live `pg_stat_user_tables` for `public.attempts` with only 10 live rows: `seq_scan = 3005`, `idx_scan = 918`, `seq_tup_read = 95889`. For `public.judgments`: `seq_scan = 255`, `idx_scan = 0`. Stats have never been reset.
* `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` on the gallery tier predicate (`packages/backend/src/profile.ts:469`, run on every signed-in `GET /v1/gallery`): `Seq Scan on attempts a ... Rows Removed by Filter: 2000` on a 2000-attempt replay.
* `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` on `packages/backend/src/store.ts:483` / `:515` (`getJudgments`, `getJudgmentRubricVersions`, reached via `trackCustody`): `Seq Scan on judgments j ... Rows Removed by Filter: 23988` to return 12 rows.
* `packages/backend/src/scoresOfRecord.ts` `JUDGING_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000`, and `trackCustody` runs once per track.
* No table in `public` has ever been analyzed or autovacuumed (`last_autovacuum IS NULL`, `last_analyze IS NULL` for every table).

**Recommended (no migration written here):** `attempts (participant_id, finalized_at)`, `judgments (attempt_id, track_id)`, and `attempt_site_claims (response_id)` for the FK check.

**Blast radius.** Every signed-in page read and every judging poll degrades linearly with total attempts across ALL candidates, not with the caller's own. At 50 concurrent sittings polling at 5 s that is 10 requests/second each scanning `judgments` three times.

**How we know it is fixed.** `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` for the three columns, both `EXPLAIN`s above show an Index Scan, and `seq_scan` on `attempts` stops climbing with traffic.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*

TEN-242.title: [P1] No statement_timeout and no lock_timeout anywhere, so one slow query pins a pool slot with no end
TEN-242.description:
**What breaks.** Nothing bounds how long a single statement may run. The handler holds one pool client for its whole duration, so a query that goes linear on a growing table, or a `FOR UPDATE` waiting behind another transaction, removes a connection from a pool of 3 (or 8) for as long as it takes. There is no ceiling and no error to alert on.

**Evidence.**

* Live `pg_settings` on the production database: `statement_timeout = 0`, `lock_timeout = 0`, `max_connections = 112`. `pg_db_role_setting` is EMPTY, so no per-role or per-database default is set either.
* Repo grep for `statement_timeout` / `lock_timeout` / `idle_in_transaction` across `*.ts`, `*.sql`, `*.tf` returns nothing in any source file. `poolConfig` (`services/api/src/context.ts:98-110`) sets only `idleTimeoutMillis` and `connectionTimeoutMillis`, which are client-side.
* `infra/terraform/variables.tf` states the design plainly: the pool IS the instance's real request concurrency.

**Blast radius.** Whole service. It is the reason the unbounded scans and the judging checkout have no natural end.

**How we know it is fixed.** `poolConfig` sets `options: '-c statement_timeout=... -c lock_timeout=...'` (with a longer explicit budget for the judging session), and a deliberately slow query returns SQLSTATE `57014` instead of holding a connection.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*

TEN-241.title: [P1] A judging run killed mid-pass is re-claimed for ever because tries is never incremented on claim
TEN-241.description:
**What breaks.** `tries` is incremented only by `recordJudgingOutcome`. A process killed mid-pass never records an outcome, so `MAX_TRIES = 3` never applies and the row is re-claimed indefinitely. The kill is routine, not exceptional: the worst-case drain is 5 attempts x 2 tracks x 3 jury x 3 retries x 120 s = 10800 s against a job timeout of 1800 s with `max_retries = 0`. The candidate sees `pending_judging` for ever, which is the original spinner defect under a new state name.

**Evidence.**

* `packages/backend/src/judging/queue.ts:196-240` `recordJudgingOutcome` is the only writer of `tries`; `claimAttemptForJudging` (`queue.ts:157-186`) does not touch it.
* `infra/terraform/judging.tf:39-43` job `timeout = 1800s`, `max_retries = 0`.
* `packages/backend/src/judging/model.ts:125` `timeoutMs: 120_000, maxRetries: 2`.
* `packages/backend/src/scoresOfRecord.ts:338-341` reports a `pending` run as `pending_judging` with a poll interval, so the client keeps asking.
* There is also no spend ceiling per attempt, per drain or per day: only a batch COUNT bounds cost (`packages/backend/src/judging/judge.ts:100`). A re-claim loop therefore has no cost backstop and no alarm.

**Blast radius.** Any attempt whose pass exceeds the job timeout. It never terminates, it re-bills the jury on every drain, and the candidate is never told.

**How we know it is fixed.** `tries` is incremented at claim time (or the lease expiry counts as a try), a row that exceeds `MAX_TRIES` becomes terminal `failed`, and a killed run reaches `failed` after three drains rather than looping.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*

TEN-240.title: [P1] The judging lease is not atomic: SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED runs outside a transaction
TEN-240.description:
**What breaks.** `claimAttemptForJudging` issues `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` with no `BEGIN`, so the row lock is released at statement end, and the `UPDATE` that marks the row `running` is a separate statement. Two runners can claim the same attempt and pay the jury twice. The lease duration makes it likely rather than theoretical: `LEASE_MS` is 600000 and the scheduler cron is `*/10`, while the worst-case pass is 2 tracks x 3 jury x 3 attempts x 120 s = 2160 s, which is 3.6x longer than the lease.

**Evidence.**

* `packages/backend/src/judging/queue.ts:157-186`: the `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and the `UPDATE` are separate statements with no surrounding transaction. `withTransaction` exists at `packages/backend/src/db.ts:19` and is not used here.
* `packages/backend/src/judging/queue.ts:76` `LEASE_MS = 600_000`; `infra/terraform/variables.tf:460-470` sets the drain cron to `*/10`.
* `services/api/src/judging.ts:103-106` asserts this cannot happen.
* Live: `judging_runs` is empty, so the path has never been exercised against real concurrency.
* The unique keys on `judgments` and `scores` stop a duplicate ROW, but they do not stop the duplicate model CALL, which is the bill.

**Blast radius.** Duplicate judge spend on every attempt that two runners race on, and duplicate rows if the gateway echoes a different model id (see the related model-id finding).

**How we know it is fixed.** The claim is one statement or one transaction, `LEASE_MS` exceeds the worst-case pass duration, and a test starting two runners against one queued attempt shows exactly one model call.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*

**What breaks.** The three end-of-sitting write panels collapse a refusal and an unreachable service into one sentence and throw the status away. A 403, a 409 or a 429 all read as the network hiccuped, try again, so the candidate retries a permanent answer forever.

**Blast radius.** The three write actions a candidate performs at the end of a sitting, including issuing and revoking a credential.

**Fixed when.** The panels use the same refused/unreachable split, print the status and the service's reason, and do not offer a retry for a refusal that will not change. A 403 on issue and on create must not produce the try again in a moment wording.

**What breaks.** The sentinel that stops the secrecy gate becoming a green light is computed over MODES, and the third mode is the committed `apps/web/public` tree, which always exists. **How to know it is fixed.** The graph is resolved with the bundler's own resolution or a real parser, `hooks/` is scanned, and adding a dynamic import of the identity module into a client file makes the test fail.

TEN-202.title: [P2] The board poll has no timeout and no overlap guard
TEN-202.description:
**What breaks.** `features/board/useBoard.ts:159` fetches with no signal, and `:131` starts a `setInterval`. The `pending` ref at `:57` counts moves only, so a tick starts a new refresh while the previous one is still open. With the missing Linear timeout, a tab accumulates hanging connections and `syncing` never clears.

**Evidence.** `features/board/useBoard.ts:57`, `:131`, `:159`.

**Blast radius.** Every open board tab, one stacked request per minute, and a spinner that never stops.

**How to know it is fixed.** An in-flight flag plus an abort signal. With a fetch stub that never resolves and fake timers advanced ten intervals, exactly one request is open.
TEN-202.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-201.title: [P2] The who parameter is not validated as a uuid, so a typo reads as a database failure
TEN-201.description:
**What breaks.** `features/people/model.ts:408` only trims and truncates `who`. `PARTICIPANT_AUTH_REF_SQL` casts `$1::uuid`, so a non-uuid makes Postgres raise, and the page prints "the exam database refused the query".

**Evidence.** `features/people/model.ts:408`, `features/people/sql.ts` `PARTICIPANT_AUTH_REF_SQL`. The surrounding comment says a hand-edited URL is not a fault condition, which is right and is not what happens here.

**Blast radius.** `/people?who=` with any typo. The store is blamed for a URL.

**How to know it is fixed.** The uuid shape is checked in `parsePeopleQuery` and the existing "no participant carries that id" sentence renders instead. One unit test with `?who=nope`.
TEN-201.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-200.title: [P2] An out of range page number renders zero matching people
TEN-200.description:
**What breaks.** `features/people/load.ts` takes the total from `rows[0]?.total ?? 0`, so a page past the last one has no rows and reports a total of zero. `features/people/PeoplePanel.tsx:227` then renders "0 matching people" for a store that holds eight, and it renders that zero as a digit through `formatCount`, bypassing the rule that a counted zero must be words.

**Evidence.** `features/people/load.ts` `loadPeoplePage` (`const total = rows[0]?.total ?? 0`), `features/people/model.ts` `parsePeopleQuery` (page is any positive integer, never clamped), `features/people/PeoplePanel.tsx:227`.

**Blast radius.** Anyone who edits the URL or follows a stale pager link. A wrong figure with no standing next to it, on the page that carries identities.

**How to know it is fixed.** The page is clamped to the page count, or the total comes from its own count and an empty page says so in words. `?page=99` renders the real total.
TEN-200.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-199.title: [P2] The share step is labelled seen by someone else and counts views the owner may have made
TEN-199.description:
**What breaks.** The funnel step "Was seen by someone else" counts rows in `share_views`, and nothing in that table can tell the owner's own view from a stranger's.

**Evidence.** `features/analytics/model.ts` `buildFunnel()`, the last step. `share_views` holds `id, share_id, viewed_on` and nothing else: no visitor id, no referrer, by design. Store today: 7 rows across 2 links, and 2 of 2 shared attempts belong to development identities.

**Blast radius.** The bottom of the sitting funnel, which is the step that would be read as proof of a loop. The step's own definition text is accurate; the label is the claim a reader takes away.

**How to know it is fixed.** The label says what the row proves, for example "the share card was served", and the definition keeps its caveat.
TEN-199.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-198.title: [P2] Nothing in the types stops a rate being taken across the funnel and cohort seam
TEN-198.description:
**What breaks.** The seam is the page's strongest claim and it is held by prose and review only. `SEAM_WORDS` states it, the panels obey it, and nothing enforces it.

**Evidence.** `features/analytics/model.ts` defines `FrontFunnelCounts` (browsing sessions, browsers, rounds) and `FunnelCounts` (participants, sittings) as plain `number` fields. `lib/measured.ts` `ratio()` takes two bare numbers. Any future call site can divide a session count by a sitting count and the type checker, the lint run and the test suite all pass. The one structural protection, that `funnel_events` carries no participant or attempt id, lives in the exam service and not here.

**Blast radius.** One careless panel and the dashboard publishes a conversion rate with no defensible denominator, which is the exact error `docs/SAMPLING.md` says the two-track design exists to prevent.

**How to know it is fixed.** The two units are distinct types (branded numbers or wrapper types) so a cross-unit ratio does not compile, or a test asserts every `ratio()` call site takes both arguments from the same count object.
TEN-198.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-197.title: [P2] A store with the funnel table missing is typed as unconfigured rather than empty
TEN-197.description:
**What breaks.** The five standing kinds are meant to be exhaustive and distinct: `unconfigured` means nobody pointed this deploy at a source and the fix is an environment variable. `app/(dashboard)/people/page.tsx` `unread()` returns `kind: "unconfigured"` for a store that IS configured and simply predates the funnel migration. That is a configured source reported as an unset variable.

**Evidence.** `app/(dashboard)/people/page.tsx`, function `unread()`, returning `{ kind: "unconfigured", reason: ... }` from a branch reached only when the database read succeeded. `lib/standing.ts` maps `unconfigured` to the label "no source configured" and to the dashed mark.

**Blast radius.** Small today, because `BrowserPanel` renders only the reason text, which is accurate. It grows the moment anything summarises that source into a standing badge or an attention row, which is what `lib/standing.ts` exists for.

**How to know it is fixed.** The state has its own kind or reuses `empty`, and no code path can label a reachable store "no source configured". A test that reads a store without `funnel_events` asserts the kind.
TEN-197.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-196.title: [P2] The KPI return cohorts and the people page use two different definitions of active
TEN-196.description:
**What breaks.** The same word means two things on two pages, and neither page says the other exists.

**Evidence.** `lib/kpi.ts` `KPI_COUNTS_SQL` builds its `activity` CTE from `attempts.started_at` and `practice_sessions.started_at` only. `features/people/sql.ts` `ACTIVE_DAYS_SQL` and `ACTIVE_WINDOWS_SQL` build theirs from four events: sitting started, sitting finalized, practice started, practice completed, and `features/people/model.ts` prints that definition on screen as the page's chosen one. A person who finalized on the day after they started counts as returning on `/people` and does not on `/kpi`.

**Blast radius.** D1 and D7 return, which are two of the six figures a funder asks for. Both are withheld today for a small cohort, so the defect is latent and lands the first time the cohort reaches twenty.

**How to know it is fixed.** One definition of an active day, shared by both queries, printed once. A fixture where a participant only finalizes on day one gives the same answer on both pages.
TEN-196.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-195.title: [P2] Analytics and KPI day buckets are cast without a timezone while people buckets are cast with one
TEN-195.description:
**What breaks.** Two pages can put the same sitting on different days, and the boundary moves with a connection setting.

**Evidence.** `features/analytics/sql.ts` uses `started_at::date` and `finalized_at::date` (`ATTEMPTS_PER_DAY_SQL`, `PRACTICE_PER_DAY_SQL`); `lib/kpi.ts` `KPI_COUNTS_SQL` does the same and compares against `current_date`. `features/people/sql.ts` pins `AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'` on every cast and explains at length why: "a day boundary that moves with a connection setting is not a measurement". The live store reports `TimeZone = GMT`, so the two agree today by accident of configuration, not by construction.

**Blast radius.** The day series on `/analytics`, the D1 and D7 cohorts on `/kpi`, and any comparison a reader makes between those and `/people`.

**How to know it is fixed.** Every cast names the zone. Run one fixture under `SET TIME ZONE 'Pacific/Auckland'` and assert the buckets do not move.
TEN-195.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-194.title: [P2] A row shaping error is reported as a database refusal
TEN-194.description:
**What breaks.** `lib/server/db.ts:70-80` runs `result.rows.map(shape)` inside the same `try` as the SQL, so a throw from `toCount` (`:110`) or `toDay` is caught by the database catch at `:82` and rendered as "The exam database refused the query". The database was fine; the shaper was wrong.

**Evidence.** `lib/server/db.ts:66-88`. A renamed column or a NULL count produces this today.

**Blast radius.** Any panel. In a repo whose central rule is that a sentence on screen must be true, this is a wrong sentence with a confident diagnosis attached, and it sends the reader to the store instead of to the code.

**How to know it is fixed.** Shape outside the transaction try, or tag the two failures apart. A shaper that throws produces a reason naming a shaping fault.
TEN-194.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-193.title: [P1] The Clerk identity fetch has no timeout, so a searched people page hangs
TEN-193.description:
**What breaks.** `lib/server/identity.ts:104` awaits `fetcher(...)` with `cache: "no-store"` and no `signal`. It is called from the search path in `features/people/load.ts` and from `resolveIdentity` at `app/(dashboard)/people/page.tsx:71`.

**Evidence.** `lib/server/identity.ts:104`. The module has a refusal state to render; nothing bounds the wait that would reach it.

**Blast radius.** `/people` with `?q=` or `?who=`, which is the point of the page.

**How to know it is fixed.** An abort signal on the fetch. With a never-resolving fetcher, `searchClerkUsers` returns its refused state inside the deadline and the no-logging test still passes.
TEN-193.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-192.title: [P1] The people table aggregates the whole store on every page view
TEN-192.description:
**What breaks.** `peoplePageSql` (`features/people/sql.ts`) leaves `matched` unfiltered when both parameters are NULL, which is the default view. `att` and `pr` then aggregate all of `attempts` and all of `practice_sessions` grouped by participant, and `count(*) OVER ()` runs over every matched row, before `LIMIT $3 OFFSET $4`. The comment above the function says the table must never fetch every participant. The rows returned are paged; the work is not.

**Evidence.** `features/people/sql.ts` `peoplePageSql`, the `matched`, `att`, `pr` and `page_rows` CTEs. The suffix predicate `auth_ref LIKE '%' || $1` also cannot use a b-tree, as the comment concedes.

**Blast radius.** `/people` is the first page to hit `statement_timeout` at scale, and it will render "the exam database refused the query", which reads as a broken deployment.

**How to know it is fixed.** Page `matched` first with a LIMIT inside the CTE, aggregate only the page, take the total as a separate cheap count. EXPLAIN the default statement against a seeded 100k participant table.
TEN-192.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-191.title: [P1] Every live score manifest is pulled and parsed on three pages with no limit
TEN-191.description:
**What breaks.** `SCORE_MANIFESTS_SQL` (`lib/truth.ts:72`) selects `attempt_id, model_manifest` for every row with `superseded_by IS NULL`, ordered, unbounded. `loadScoreManifests` runs on `/` (`app/(dashboard)/page.tsx:70`), `/truth` and `/money`, all `force-dynamic`. Each manifest is a JSON blob parsed per row per render in `lib/manifest.ts`.

**Evidence.** `lib/truth.ts:72`, `lib/server/read.ts` `loadScoreManifests`, and the three page call sites. One live row today, so nothing shows yet.

**Blast radius.** The overview is the first page opened and it degrades in proportion to success.

**How to know it is fixed.** The arithmetic is aggregated in SQL, or the read carries a LIMIT and the page says in words that it counted the most recent N. Seed 50k rows and hold the read inside a fixed budget.
TEN-191.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-189.title: [P1] The pool is capped at two while the analytics page fires ten reads at once
TEN-189.description:
**What breaks.** Pool `max: 2` (`lib/server/db.ts:30`). `app/(dashboard)/analytics/page.tsx:59` awaits the sink read, then `:62-73` runs `Promise.all` over ten loaders, each holding a client for three round trips. Ten reads serialise into five waves. With `statement_timeout: 10_000` the worst case is about 50 seconds before anything renders, and the checkout queue has no deadline of its own.

**Evidence.** `lib/server/db.ts:30`, `app/(dashboard)/analytics/page.tsx:59-73`. `/people` has the same shape at `app/(dashboard)/people/page.tsx:60-71`.

**Blast radius.** The two heaviest pages, exactly when the store is slow.

**How to know it is fixed.** The cap is above the widest fan-out, or the analytics reads are batched into fewer statements, plus a per page deadline. Count concurrent checkouts during one `/analytics` render.
TEN-189.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-188.title: [P1] The middleware asks Clerk for the user on every request, so normal use can rate limit the dashboard
TEN-188.description:
**What breaks.** `middleware.ts:47` calls `users.getUser` on every matched request with no cache. The matcher at `:68` excludes only `_next/static`, `_next/image` and `favicon.ico`, so every RSC navigation payload, every file under `public/`, and every 60 second `/api/board` poll per open tab is one Clerk Backend API call.

**Evidence.** `middleware.ts:47` and `:68`. Clerk BAPI limits are per instance and in the low hundreds per 10 second window. The first 429 lands in the catch at `:38` and renders as a denial, so the failure presents as a lockout that blames the allowlist.

**Blast radius.** The whole app, worse with each tab left open.

**How to know it is fixed.** Memoise the email per user id for 30 to 60 seconds in module scope, the trick `boardCache` already uses, or carry the email in the session claim. Count `getUser` calls across one navigation and assert it is one.
TEN-188.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-187.title: [P1] The Clerk lookup in the middleware has no deadline
TEN-187.description:
**What breaks.** `middleware.ts:32-33` awaits `clerkClient()` then `client.users.getUser(userId)` with no timeout. The SDK sets none. This runs before anything else on every gated request, so a slow Clerk is a hard stop ahead of the database and the page.

**Evidence.** `middleware.ts:32-33`; the same pattern at `lib/server/admin.ts:50-51`.

**Blast radius.** Every page and both API routes. `/sign-in`, `/denied` and `/locked` still answer, so the deploy looks half alive rather than down.

**How to know it is fixed.** The lookup races an abort at a few seconds and a timeout is a refusal with its own sentence. With a client that never resolves, the request completes inside the deadline.
TEN-187.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-186.title: [P1] A Clerk outage renders as not on the allowlist, which points the reader at the wrong fix
TEN-186.description:
**What breaks.** `middleware.ts:38-41` catches a failed Clerk lookup and returns `null`; `:47` feeds that to `isAllowedEmail`, which cannot tell "no email" from "Clerk did not answer", and the request is rewritten to `/denied`. `lib/server/admin.ts:56-60` does the same and returns a 403 reading "this account is not on the allowlist".

**Evidence.** `middleware.ts:38-48`, `lib/server/admin.ts:50-60`.

**Blast radius.** Every admin at once during any Clerk incident, and the recovery action the copy asks for (edit `ADMIN_ALLOWED_EMAILS`) cannot help. Failing closed is right. Naming the wrong cause is the defect, and it is the same error this repo refuses everywhere else: an unreadable source must say it is unreadable.

**How to know it is fixed.** A third state for unreachable with its own sentence. A throwing Clerk client produces it; an allowlist miss still produces denied.
TEN-186.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-185.title: [P1] The pg pool has no error listener, so one idle client reset can end the process
TEN-185.description:
**What breaks.** There is no `pool.on("error", ...)` anywhere. pg re-emits an idle client's error on the Pool, and an EventEmitter with no `error` listener throws, which in the Next server is an uncaught exception.

**Evidence.** `lib/server/db.ts:26-33`; a grep for `pool.on` over `lib`, `app` and `features` is empty. Managed Postgres reaping idle sessions, a failover, or a NAT idle drop all trigger it. `idleTimeoutMillis: 10_000` narrows the window and does not close it.

**Blast radius.** The whole dashboard, every reader, until the platform restarts the instance.

**How to know it is fixed.** A listener that logs and does nothing else. Against a throwaway local Postgres: check a client in, terminate its backend, assert the process survives and the next `readRows` answers.
TEN-185.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-184.title: [P1] A hung board read pins the in-flight promise for the life of the process
TEN-184.description:
**What breaks.** `lib/server/boardCache.ts:44-52` stores the in-flight promise and clears it only in `finally`. A read that never settles is never cleared, so every later `/board` render and every 60 second `/api/board` poll joins the same dead promise. The board stays down until redeploy.

**Evidence.** `lib/server/boardCache.ts:41-52`, together with the missing abort signal at `lib/linearBoard.ts:190`.

**Blast radius.** `/board` and both board routes, for every reader, until the instance restarts.

**How to know it is fixed.** After a never-resolving read, the next call starts a fresh read. A stub that hangs once and then answers must produce an answer on the second call.
TEN-184.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-183.title: [P0] Board calls to Linear carry no abort signal, so a slow Linear hangs the board
TEN-183.description:
**What breaks.** `lib/linearBoard.ts:190` calls `fetchImpl(LINEAR_ENDPOINT, ...)` with no `signal` and no timeout, reached from `:233`, `:239` and `:291`. `loadBoard` pages sequentially up to `BOARD_MAX_PAGES = 20` (`:238`), so the worst case is 21 chained unbounded awaits.

**Evidence.** `lib/linear.ts:227` already does this correctly with `AbortSignal.timeout(SPRINT_TIMEOUT_MS)`; the board module never got it. `app/api/board/move/route.ts:52` awaits `readBoard()` before the mutation, so a drag hangs on the same read.

**Blast radius.** `/board`, `GET /api/board`, `POST /api/board/move`.

**How to know it is fixed.** `callLinear` takes the same abort signal as the sprint read. With a fetch stub that never resolves, `readBoard()` reaches its error state inside the deadline.
TEN-183.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-182.title: [P0] The pg pool has no connect timeout, so an unreachable store hangs every page
TEN-182.description:
**What breaks.** `lib/server/db.ts:30` builds the pool with `max`, `idleTimeoutMillis` and `statement_timeout`, and no `connectionTimeoutMillis`. pg defaults that to 0, which means wait forever. `statement_timeout` only applies once a connection exists, so it guards nothing here. `await getPool(url).connect()` at `lib/server/db.ts:64` is an unbounded await on every page.

**Evidence.** `lib/server/db.ts:26-33` and `:64`. The catch at `:65` holds the honest "the exam database could not be reached" state and never runs while the connect is pending. Best fit for the 95 second hang already observed: the OS TCP timer, not ours, ends the wait.

**Blast radius.** Every dashboard page and both board API routes. The failure is a hang, so the empty-state vocabulary never gets to speak.

**How to know it is fixed.** `connectionTimeoutMillis` set to a few seconds. Point the URL at an unrouteable address (not a closed port, which fails fast), load `/kpi`, assert the error state renders inside the deadline.
TEN-182.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-154.title: A Vercel preview cannot verify any hosted-mode change: no preview env vars, deployment protection on, and the service's CORS allowlist names only staging
TEN-154.description:
Found while trying to verify PR #46 against a Vercel PREVIEW. The preview cannot test anything
that talks to the exam service, for three independent reasons. Any one of them alone would be
enough.

1. **The Preview environment has no environment variables.** `vercel env ls` on `ailx-staging`
   shows every variable scoped to **Production only** — `AILX_BACKEND`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_AILX_API_BASE`,
   `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `AILX_AUTH`, all of them. The single exception is
   `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`. So a preview builds WITHOUT `AILX_BACKEND=1`: it has none of the seven
   database-reading pages, no API base and no Clerk. It is a different product.
2. **Deployment Protection is on.** The preview alias redirects a browser to `vercel.com/login`,
   so no agent and no reviewer can open it without a Vercel session or an automation bypass token.
   No bypass secret is configured.
3. **The service's CORS allowlist names two origins.** Cloud Run `AILX_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is
   `https://rryoung98.github.io,https://ailx-staging.vercel.app`. A preview URL is neither, so
   every authenticated call from a preview would be blocked at the preflight even with the env
   vars and the protection sorted.

**Consequence.** No frontend change that touches the hosted mode can be proven before it is
merged and deployed to production staging. Tonight that meant PR #46 — two candidate-visible
identity defects — could only be verified against a LOCAL hosted build with a stubbed service.
That worked and was conclusive, but it is not the deployment.

Ways out, cheapest first:

* scope the non-secret variables (`AILX_BACKEND`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_AILX_BACKEND`,
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_AILX_API_BASE`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` — the last two are public by
  design) to Preview as well as Production;
* turn on Protection Bypass for Automation and hold the token where CI and an agent can read it;
* allow the project's preview wildcard origin in `AILX_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, or point previews at a
  disposable service.

The third one is a deliberate security boundary and deserves the most thought — a wildcard there
is not free.

---

**Decision recorded 2026-09-05.** Not fixed tonight, deliberately. The three halves are not equally
cheap and should not be done in one patch:

* **The env scoping is independently fixable and the cheapest of the three.** Every variable is
  Production-only today. Scoping `AILX_BACKEND`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_AILX_BACKEND`,
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_AILX_API_BASE` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` to Preview as well would
  already turn a preview from "a different product" into "the same product it cannot phone home
  from". The last two are publishable by design, so nothing secret moves. Do this one first; it
  needs no security argument.
* Protection Bypass for Automation is a second, separate step.
* **Widening** `AILX_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` **to preview origins is a real security boundary and needs a**
  **decision, not a patch.** A wildcard there is not free. A disposable service for previews is the
  alternative worth costing.
TEN-154.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-151.title: Two copy lines tell a signed-in candidate they have no account: /exam's access pill and the daily result screen
TEN-151.description:
Small, but it is what a signed-in candidate reads tonight (staging, 2026-09-05).

* /exam header pill: "sign in to sit a scored run" — `apps/web/lib/mode.ts` `examAccessCopy()`
  returns this whenever Clerk is enabled, regardless of whether the reader is signed in. A
  signed-in candidate is told to do the thing they just did.
* /daily result screen: "Your streak lives on this device only: clear your browser data and it
  is gone. There is no account to lose it to." — said to a candidate who has an account, on a
  deployment that has accounts.

Both are unconditional strings on identity-aware pages. Fixing them needs the identity seam from
<issue id="e1efbe6b-1ebe-4853-a3e8-316671de1fba" href="https://linear.app/tenken/issue/TEN-148/progress-refuses-a-signed-in-candidate-identity-required-reads-fire">TEN-148</issue>, so they are worth doing in the same pass.
TEN-151.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-150.title: funnel_events.identified is false on every row by construction, including signed_in — decide whether the column should exist
TEN-150.description:
Checked in the staging store 2026-09-05. `funnel_events.identified` is `false` on every row ever
written, including the `signed_in` row emitted tonight the moment an account arrived.

It cannot be anything else. `apps/web/lib/data/funnel.ts` `browserSend()` posts with
`credentials: "omit"` and no identity header, deliberately ("Anonymous by construction"), which
is the promise docs/KPI.md makes. So the service has nothing to set the column from, and the
column is dead weight that reads as a fact.

Two ways out, and it needs a decision rather than a patch:

* delete the column and say in docs/KPI.md that the funnel cannot separate signed-in traffic; or
* keep it and define exactly what would set it (e.g. the service marking a batch that arrived
  with a valid bearer, which would break the anonymity promise and must be argued for).

Either way `signed_in` is currently a step that records that SOMEBODY signed in during a
session, on a row that says nobody was identified. As long as both exist unexplained, an
analytics reader will draw the wrong conclusion.
TEN-150.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-144.title: Funnel: visit_started is not emitted on six top-level routes, so D1/D7 undercounts return
TEN-144.description:
**Found by driving deployed staging ([https://ailx-staging.vercel.app](<https://ailx-staging.vercel.app>)) on 2026-09-05, first night** `/v1/events` **was live.**

`visit_started` is emitted by `session()` inside `apps/web/lib/data/funnel.ts`, on the first event a page asks the emitter for. A route that emits no other step therefore emits nothing at all — no client id is minted, no session is opened, no row is posted.

Verified in the browser on the deployed site. Six routes are dark:
`/progress`, `/report`, `/gallery`, `/world`, `/validate`, `/methodology`.
After loading each one and waiting past the flush window, `localStorage["ailx.funnel.client.v1"]` was `null` and `funnel_events` gained zero rows.

**Why it matters.** docs/KPI.md step 1 says `visit_started` means "a browser opened Foray", and the admin analytics page words it "a browser opened Foray at all". Neither is what the code counts. Worse, `/progress` is the destination the practice and daily result screens link to ("See your progress"), so it is the most likely *return* surface — and D1/D7 is derived from client ids that emitted something. A player who practises on day 0 and comes back on day 1 to look at their streak emits nothing, and is counted as not returned. D1 is biased low at exactly the place the product expects return.

**Measured in this run.** 12 browser sessions opened the site. `funnel_events` holds 10 `visit_started`. The two missing are the sessions that only read non-instrumented pages (one of them six page loads).

**Fix (pushed, not merged):** branch `w/funnel-visit` on rryoung98/ailx, commit `633c103`.

* `funnel().visit()` — a new entry point that only opens the session.
* `apps/web/components/FunnelVisit.tsx`, mounted in `app/layout.tsx` outside `AuthShell` so it does not depend on Clerk being configured.
* Four tests in `apps/web/test/funnelSurfaces.test.tsx`: one visit and nothing else, one visit across remounts and a reload, no interference with a real step, and silence with no backend.
* `pnpm test` green (3138 passed, 38 skipped). `pnpm lint` reports no new diagnostics.

TEN-111.title: HIGH: the T1 upload path can OOM a Cloud Run instance — 25MB double-buffered, no rate limit, 512Mi at concurrency 80
TEN-111.description:
From the 2026-09-04 backend review (/Users/rickyyoung/GitHub/ailx-backend-review-2026-09-04.md, finding **D2**, BUG/HIGH).

* `services/api/src/context.ts:42-43` — `MAX_RAW_BODY_BYTES = T1_LIMITS.maxTotalBytes` = 25 MB.
* `services/api/src/context.ts:130-160` — `readCappedBody` buffers every chunk in `chunks[]` then copies into `out`: transiently TWO copies of the body.
* `services/api/src/app.ts:341-352` — `POST /v1/attempts/:id/site` is `{ rawBody: true }` with **no** `limit`. `services/api/src/rateLimit.ts` covers only score/finalize and the model routes.
* `infra/terraform/variables.tf:129` memory default `512Mi` (not overridden in `env/staging.tfvars`), `:164` concurrency default `80`, `:153` max_instances 4.

**Measured** against the repo's own `packages/backend/dist/t1/snapshot.js` with 21 stored/incompressible files totalling 24 MB: baseline 66 MB rss; 1 upload in flight 178 MB; 4 in flight 307 MB — roughly 46 MB retained per in-flight upload. About 8-9 concurrent uploads OOM-kill an instance, taking every other in-flight sitting on it with it. `GET /v1/attempts/:id/site/export` has the same shape: it repacks a whole ZIP in memory.

**Fix.** Rate-limit `POST /v1/attempts/:id/site` per identity (it is the only unlimited rawBody route), set an explicit memory value well above 512Mi for the upload path, and lower concurrency or stream the body to the snapshot store instead of double-buffering.

TEN-110.title: HIGH: the served score is the candidate's mirrored number, not the score of record
TEN-110.description:
From the 2026-09-04 backend review (/Users/rickyyoung/GitHub/ailx-backend-review-2026-09-04.md, finding **C1**, BUG/HIGH).

Every candidate-facing and PUBLIC surface derives its number by projecting the candidate's own mirrored session log. No surface reads the `scores` table.

* `packages/backend/src/aggregates.ts:39-52` + `shapeOf` at `:81-89` -> `collectWorldAggregates` (`:138`) -> `handleWorldAggregates` (`:163`), an **unauthenticated public statistic**.
* `packages/backend/src/share.ts:136` -> `:188` `buildSharePayload`; `packages/report/src/share.ts:219,224,269` freeze `band` and the four per-track numbers into the share payload. Gallery and moderation cards read that payload (`gallery.ts:139`, `moderation.ts:113`).
* `packages/backend/src/practice.ts:391-397` — the personal progression chart.

The candidate can write those rows: `appendResponse` accepts any JSON payload on their own open attempt (`store.ts:682-686`).

**Impact.** A candidate can publish a fabricated band/score on their share card and gallery entry, and move the public world aggregate. The service DOES issue a real score row (`finalize.ts:280-318`, `judging/worker.ts:374`) and never compares the two. `scoredBy` never leaves `finalize.ts:287` — grep finds it nowhere in `@ailx/report`, so the served payload carries no provenance label either. The only mitigation in code today is a comment calling the aggregate "advisory" (`aggregates.ts:18-20`), which is not a property of the API.

**Fix.** Serve the `scores` row on every surface that states a number; failing that, exclude the mirrored number from the public aggregate and label it in the payload (not in a comment). Reconciling the two and recording disagreement would also satisfy the audit story.

TEN-181.title: [P0] The complete score of record gate clears on a single track manifest
TEN-181.description:
**What breaks.** The truth panel answers "A score of record measures what the spec says it measures" YES, and the route gate "One complete score of record" reads PASSED, from one score row covering one track. The same page declares T3 (160 points) unvalidated and T4 issuing no points.

**Evidence (live store plus the repo's own pure functions, run 2026-09-07).**

* `scores` holds exactly 1 live row: `track_id = t2`, `model_manifest.trackPoints = 80`, 4 components, every one `status = measured`, `partial = false`.
* `readScores()` returns `liveScores 1, completeScores 1, partialScores 0, latest total 80, measured 80, complete true`.
* `buildTruthChecks()` renders `YES | A score of record measures what the spec says it measures | points in the most recently scored sitting=80, of them measured=80`.
* `buildGtmRoute()` renders `passed | One complete score of record`. `lib/gtm.ts:270` reads the truth verdict by claim, so the two cannot disagree and both are wrong together.
* `lib/manifest.ts` computes coverage from the manifest's own `trackPoints`, which is per track. Nothing compares it to the instrument and nothing checks which tracks the sitting was dealt. `attempt_decks` for that attempt names t2 only.
* The premise in the `lib/manifest.ts` header is stale: it says the pipeline writes `partial: true` on every score it can produce. The stored row says `partial: false`.

**Blast radius.** The flagship check on `/truth`, the gate row on `/money`, and the "Gates cleared on the route" tile on the overview. A release gate that clears itself is worse than no gate.

**How to know it is fixed.** Coverage is computed against the instrument the sitting claims, not against one track's own denominator. A fixture with a single complete t2 manifest renders partial or unknown and does not clear the gate.
TEN-181.project: AILX — 6-week sprint to a defensible instrument

TEN-180.title: [P0] Development identities are counted as registered users and their sittings as sittings
TEN-180.description:
**What breaks.** Every headline figure counts `dev:` asserted development identities as real people. No query anywhere excludes them.

**Evidence (live store, read only, 2026-09-07).**

* `participants` holds 8 rows: 4 with an `auth_ref` under the `dev:` prefix, 4 under `clerk:`.
* `attempts`: 10 rows, 9 of them belonging to `dev:` participants. Real participant sittings: 1.
* Finalized attempts: 6, of which 5 are `dev:`. Real finalized sittings: 1.
* Credentials on `dev:` attempts: 3 of 4. Share links on `dev:` attempts: 2 of 2. Practice sessions: 1 of 7 is `dev:`.
* `lib/kpi.ts` `KPI_COUNTS_SQL` counts `participants WHERE auth_ref IS NOT NULL` as "Registered users" and `count(*) FROM attempts` as "Sittings started". Neither filters the prefix.
* The repo knows the distinction already: `features/people/model.ts:341` `providerOf()` splits `clerk:` from asserted, and the public contract has `isDevUserId` (`packages/contract/src/identity.ts:52`). The per-row table says "no Clerk account, asserted by the service". The aggregates ignore all of it.
* Downstream: `lib/truth.ts` renders "People have completed a sitting: YES" on 6 completions of which 5 are development. `lib/tiles.ts` renders the same counts as overview tiles. The analytics funnel, track progress, share loop and day series all inherit it.

**Blast radius.** Every counted figure except the front-of-funnel browser counts and practice. This is the number a founder would quote in a funding conversation, and it is wrong in the flattering direction.

**How to know it is fixed.** One predicate in one place, applied to every participant-derived query: exclude asserted identities from the counted figures, or count them and render "of them development" beside each. A test that seeds one `dev:` and one `clerk:` participant asserts the headline count is one, not two.

TEN-239.title: [P1] The finalize judging kick takes a second pool client and holds it across the whole jury run
TEN-239.description:
**What breaks.** `handleFinalize` awaits the judging kick while the request still holds its own pool client, and the kick checks out a SECOND client and keeps it through every model call. With the default pool of 3, three concurrent finalizes deadlock on the second checkout; with pool 8, eight do. This is the first thing that falls over under real load, and it takes down candidates who are still mid-sitting on the same instance.

**Evidence.**

* `packages/backend/src/handlers.ts:642-655` awaits `ctx.judging.kick` on `ctx.db` with no `offConnection`.
* `services/api/src/judging.ts:99-118` `run()`: `const { db, release } = await checkout()` ... `await drainJudgingQueue(deps, 1)` ... `finally { release() }`. The client is released only after the whole pass.
* `services/api/src/context.ts:112` `DEFAULT_POOL_MAX = 3`; `context.ts:106-107` `connectionTimeoutMillis: 10_000`.
* `packages/backend/src/judging/model.ts:125` `timeoutMs: 120_000, maxRetries: 2`. One jury member is up to 3 x 120 s on that held connection.
* The repo already enforces this exact rule elsewhere: `packages/backend/src/lease.ts:1-33` and the `guardHeld` port wrapper at `lease.ts:203`. The judge client is not a guarded port.
* `packages/backend/src/judging/runner.ts` header claims "IT HOLDS NO POOL CLIENT WHILE A MODEL IS SPEAKING". That is true of the request's client only.

**Blast radius.** Every route on the affected instance, including `POST /responses` inside a live sitting. Cloud Run queues rather than sheds, so the failure is a 500 after the 10 s acquire timeout.

**How we know it is fixed.** The judging pass uses its own pool or a fresh client, or releases around each model call. A load test of N concurrent finalizes shows request latency flat while the passes run.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*
