TEN-238.title: [P0] Judging is disabled in every committed environment, so no sitting can ever receive a T3 score or a composite
TEN-238.description:
**What breaks.** `judge_enabled` is false in both tfvars and in the variable default, and all of `judging.tf` is count-gated on it. So no judge Cloud Run Job, no Cloud Scheduler and no judge service account exist anywhere, and the service receives no `AILX_JUDGE_*` env. Every finalized T1 or T3 track ends terminal `unscored` / `judging_failed` with reason `unconfigured`. The composite requires all three scored tracks, so no candidate can be issued a composite at all. This is the same shape as the known no-caller defect: the fix shipped in code and not in deployment.

**Evidence.**

* `infra/terraform/env/staging.tfvars:55` `judge_enabled = false`; `infra/terraform/env/resilient-staging.tfvars:49` the same; `infra/terraform/variables.tf:310` default `false`.
* `infra/terraform/judging.tf` gates the job, the scheduler and the SA on that variable.
* `packages/backend/src/judging/*` refuses with `unconfigured` when `AILX_JUDGE_BASE_URL` is unset (README section 6.1), and `packages/backend/src/scoresOfRecord.ts` turns that into a terminal `judging_failed`.
* README section 5.2: the composite is withheld unless all three scored tracks have a score of record.
* Live: `judging_runs` is empty on the production database.
* The in-process kick (`services/api/src/judging.ts`) is detached work under `cpu_idle = true` and `min_instances = 0`, so it is not a substitute for the scheduler.

**Blast radius.** Every hosted candidate. T2 gets a number; T1 and T3 never do; the composite is never issued.

**How we know it is fixed.** `judge_enabled = true` in the environment the frontend points at, the Cloud Run Job and scheduler exist, and a finalized sitting reaches `state: scored` for T3 without an operator running anything by hand.

*Filed from a read-only review of* `ailx-backend` *@* `72db4e6` *(main), 2026-09-07.*

TEN-237.title: [P0] resilient-staging serves assert-only dev auth on a service bound to allUsers
TEN-237.description:
**What breaks.** `resilient-staging` runs `AILX_AUTH=dev`, so one request header IS any participant. That includes the six `/v1/model/*` routes, which spend the provider key sealed against that identity. This is the <issue id="3a338b1d-b8f0-4092-ad54-b68d46aa29c3" href="https://linear.app/tenken/issue/TEN-108/critical-staging-cloud-run-runs-asserted-dev-auth-with-allusers">TEN-108</issue> incident repeated on the new project.

**Evidence.**

* `infra/terraform/env/resilient-staging.tfvars:14` `auth_mode = "dev"`.
* `infra/terraform/run.tf:38-40` auto-injects `AILX_ALLOW_INSECURE_DEV_AUTH = "1"` whenever `auth_mode == "dev"`. That cancels the guard in `packages/backend/src/auth.ts:117-124` that otherwise refuses dev auth under `NODE_ENV=production`.
* `infra/terraform/run.tf:260` binds `allUsers` to `roles/run.invoker`.
* Measured read-only on 2026-09-07: `GET /v1/progress` with an asserted `x-ailx-dev-user` header against `https://ailx-backend-106323225578.us-central1.run.app` returned **200** with a full progress payload. The same request against the live `tenken-staging` service returned **401**.
* `infra/terraform/env/staging.tfvars:11` records the identical prior incident (<issue id="3a338b1d-b8f0-4092-ad54-b68d46aa29c3" href="https://linear.app/tenken/issue/TEN-108/critical-staging-cloud-run-runs-asserted-dev-auth-with-allusers">TEN-108</issue>).

Note: the probe may have created one participant row keyed `review-probe` on that service.

**Blast radius.** Anyone who can reach that URL. It is the deployment Terraform actually applies to, so it is the one the frontend is most likely pointed at next.

**How we know it is fixed.** `resilient-staging.tfvars` says `auth_mode = "clerk"`, or `run.tf` stops auto-injecting `AILX_ALLOW_INSECURE_DEV_AUTH`, and the same probe returns 401.

TEN-127.title: Only the LAST failed track can be retried — T2 stays unscored forever
TEN-127.description:
**Observed 2026-09-04, live run** `856b850c-51ac-4a1a-82a5-24deb8df66ae`**.**

`scoreRetryRef` in `apps/web/app/exam/page.tsx` holds ONE `{attemptId, trackId, artifact}`. T2 failed first (409), then T3 failed and OVERWROTE it. The single **Retry scoring** button therefore rescored T3 only. T2's retry, and its error banner, were silently lost — the hub showed just the T3 error, then no error at all.

Result: a completed, finalized run with 3 of 4 tracks scored and no way in the UI to score the fourth. The report never unlocks (see the linked report issue).

**Fix direction:** keep a per-track queue of failed scores and retry all of them; show one banner per unscored track.
